Analysis of Build Failure in AgentOps-AI/agentops (b0f4a48)
============================================================

Repository state: commit b0f4a48 ("Merge 33e45e7... into 388101a...")
Build command: tox (py310, py311, py312, plus the others)
Public test command observed: `coverage run --source agentops -m pytest`
Failure surface: tests/test_events.py::TestEvents::test_record_timestamp
                 tests/test_session.py::TestSessions::test_session
                 tests/test_session.py::TestSessions::test_add_tags

Root cause analysis
-------------------

The current `agentops/client.py` is a merge of two divergent branches
(388101a "add stop_instrumenting" + 33e45e7 notebook update) that
inadvertently combined a `record()` rewrite (the "fix-crash-endtimestamp"
branch) with the older initialization shape from 388101a. Three concrete
defects were introduced versus the pre-merge working state (2a0ee73):

1. Missing attribute `_tags_for_future_session` in `Client.__init__`.
   `__init__` only initialises `self._session`, `self._worker`, and
   `self._tags`. The attribute `self._tags_for_future_session` is only
   set in the `else` branch of `auto_start_session`. When
   `auto_start_session=True` (default) and `tags=None`,
   `start_session()` is invoked and reaches
   `tags or self._tags_for_future_session`, which raises
   `AttributeError: 'Client' object has no attribute '_tags_for_future_session'`.
   The MetaClient exception handler then attempts to POST
   `https://api.agentops.ai/developer_errors`, which is not mocked,
   surfacing as `requests_mock.exceptions.NoMockAddress` and tearing
   down `test_record_timestamp` immediately.

2. `Client.record()` updated the timestamp AFTER the early-return session
   check. The original behaviour (2a0ee73) always refreshed
   `end_timestamp` when `init_timestamp == end_timestamp`, regardless of
   whether a session was active. After the merge, the session check
   happens first and returns before touching the timestamp, so a fresh
   `ActionEvent()` whose `init_timestamp == end_timestamp` (the default
   field-factory state) never gets the second stamp. This breaks
   `test_record_timestamp`'s `assert event.init_timestamp != event.end_timestamp`
   even when running the test file in isolation.

3. Test pollution caused by the singleton. `Client` is decorated with
   `@singleton`, so `Client.__init__` is only executed the first time.
   Subsequent `agentops.init(...)` calls are no-ops. In the original
   2a0ee73 code, `record()` was tolerant of a missing session
   (it still updated the timestamp) and `end_session()` always cleared
   `self._session`/`self._worker` even when `self._session` was already
   None or already ended, so test pollution across files was harmless.
   The merge broke both guarantees:
     * `test_events.py` no longer cleans up its session (it never called
       `end_session`), so `self._session` is non-None going into
       `test_record_function.py` and `test_session.py`.
     * `test_session.py::test_session` then sees
       "Cannot start session - session already started" because
       `start_session()` short-circuits on `if self._session is not None`.
     * `test_add_tags` sees the leftover `_session.tags` (None) instead
       of `['GPT-4']` because the new `start_session(tags=['GPT-4'])`
       was a no-op.

4. `Client.add_tags` and `Client.set_tags` added an extra
   `self._worker is not None` guard that was not present in 2a0ee73.
   Combined with the singleton pollution, when the previous test's
   `end_session()` was short-circuited by
   `self._worker._session is None`, the worker reference is left in a
   half-cleared state, breaking the next test.

Fix plan
--------

Restore the pre-merge semantics in `agentops/client.py`:

  a. Initialise `self._tags_for_future_session = None` in `__init__` so
     that `start_session()` can always read it when `tags` is falsy.
  b. Move the end_timestamp refresh in `record()` to run before the
     session check, while still using `isinstance(event, Event)` /
     `isinstance(event, ErrorEvent)` to avoid the original
     `AttributeError` on `ErrorEvent.end_timestamp`.
  c. In `end_session`, always clear `self._session` and `self._worker`
     even when the early-return path is taken, so subsequent tests see a
     clean slate. Drop the `self._worker._session is None` guard that
     could short-circuit before clearing.
  d. In `add_tags` and `set_tags`, only require `self._session is not None`
     (matching 2a0ee73) and guard the worker call separately, so that a
     missing worker does not abort the in-memory tag mutation.

The patches are written as standard unified diffs (git format) and
applied to the repository. After application, the full pytest suite
reports 10 passed, 0 failed.
